finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. The OWNER check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. The caller is any authenticated user with no OWNER role, and the tenant path parameter is attacker-chosen.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive wipe of the tenant's data

trace.note: requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and does not throw (the javadoc says so)
The boolean result is ignored, with no if, return or throw

finding.guards_checked: No other guard on the path. checkRole() is used in export() but not here. There is no tenant-ownership check and no middleware visible in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: requireRole (Admin.java:14) only returns a boolean and its result is discarded at line 26; the throwing checkRole (line 18) is used only in export(); no other filter, middleware or annotation exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: At src/Admin.java:26 the bare call requireRole(u, "OWNER") returns a boolean that is discarded, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike export() at line 32, which calls the throwing checkRole.

finding.claim: Authorization is not scoped to the tenant. The OWNER role is a global string on the user and is never tied to the {t} tenant. A user who is OWNER of any tenant can export (or wipe) every other tenant's data (cross-tenant IDOR).
finding.source: POST /tenants/{t}/export. The caller is an OWNER of their own tenant, and the tenant path parameter is attacker-chosen.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33, exporting another tenant's data

trace.note: User holds only a flat Set<String> of roles, with no tenant binding
checkRole tests role membership only and never compares the tenant

finding.guards_checked: checkRole enforces correctly (it throws), but only on the role. No tenant/owner comparison exists in this file. If the roles are tenant-scoped upstream, this finding would not apply, but nothing in the repo shows that.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (Admin.java:18-22) throws correctly but only checks a global role string; no tenant comparison. (Note: wipe at line 26 uses requireRole, whose boolean result is discarded, so wipe has no authorization at all.)
verdict.reason: Admin.java:32 calls checkRole(u,"OWNER"), which at lines 18-22 only tests membership in the flat Set<String> roles (line 4), then line 33 exports the request-supplied tenant, so any OWNER of any tenant can export other tenants' data; the repo contains only this file, so no upstream tenant scoping is visible.
